reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes the BitConnectX/BCCX coin offering, predicts steep price gains and describes accumulating BitConnect coins to buy into the ICO while showing BitConnect's lending and wallet dashboard. A Georgia securities order specifically identifies BitConnectX as an offering instituted by BitConnect, the operation whose investment scheme and misleading promotion are documented by U.S. authorities. The separate CannaSOS and Storjica presales are not treated as part of that finding.

opening.argument: Judge the price discussion as speculative commentary, not a promise. The speaker explicitly says he is not a financial advisor and presents his view as how he is feeling [ASR_0001]. He does not know the launch price [ASR_0002], and even his hope of nearly doubling his holdings ends with “We'll see what happens” [ASR_0005]. Those qualifications matter: the projected prices may be optimistic, but the cited material does not establish that he guarantees them or claims special knowledge.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening quotes price targets, but the speaker calls one a “target,” guesses at the ticker, and admits he does not know the ICO price [ASR_0002]. His plan to invest is personal and expressly tentative [ASR_0005]. The asserted securities order is not among the supplied video sources; these quotes alone do not establish what an outside authority found or turn a conditional forecast into a guaranteed return.

citations.quote: target for February 2018 is 30 USD for BCC X I guess is going to be the ticker symbol
hopefully in a couple days I can Almost double that amount that I've got there in my wallet. We'll see what happens

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A disclaimer and uncertain wording do not erase the pitch. The speaker relays sharply rising target prices [ASR_0002], says he is accumulating coins specifically to buy the ICO [ASR_0004], and hopes to nearly double his wallet amount [ASR_0005]. The defense identifies uncertainty, but it does not explain away the video's purchase-and-appreciation message.

opening.argument: This is substantially a walkthrough of what the speaker sees and does. He calls the lending section “a quick review of how the BitConnect lending platform works” [ASR_0003], distinguishes his own profits from referral bonuses [ASR_0004], and explains exchange-order controls while placing his own order [ASR_0005]. For the roadmap, he credits another video and says he will not play it [ASR_0001]. A judge should distinguish showing an account workflow and discussing a third-party roadmap from claiming that the projected results are assured.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The title's “ICO Picks” [TITLE_0001] and the quoted price targets show the subject matter, but neither proves the roadmap is the speaker's own verified promise. He identifies the roadmap as material found in someone else's video [ASR_0001]. His wallet activity likewise shows what he says he is doing, not a completed BitConnectX purchase by a viewer [ASR_0004]. The outside order invoked in the opening is not itself provided as a source here.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The demonstration is also an actionable funding path: the speaker says to build up BitConnect coins to buy the BitConnectX ICO [ASR_0004], shows buying coins [ASR_0005], and states his intention to invest them in the ICO [ASR_0005]. Attributing the roadmap to another video does not neutralize his own use of its rising price targets [ASR_0002]. No viewer purchase needs to be shown for this to function as promotion.

opening.argument: The concrete activity shown is an exchange transaction and discussion of several token offerings, not evidence that a viewer surrendered funds to BitConnectX. The speaker describes an order being placed for BitConnect coins [ASR_0005] and says he is building a balance for a future ICO investment [ASR_0005]. He also discusses a separate marketplace-oriented coin and its minimum purchase [ASR_0006]. Those are observable purchases and proposed purchases; they do not, by themselves, establish a guaranteed payout, a downline-income requirement, or a completed BitConnectX purchase by anyone watching.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening connects the exchange activity to the intended ICO purchase, but intention is not a completed viewer transaction: the speaker says he is building coins to invest “in two days” [ASR_0005]. Its price-target quote reports projections, not proof that those prices were paid or guaranteed [ASR_0002]. The claimed external finding cannot be assessed from a cited order because no order is supplied among the primary materials.

Discussion of a separate marketplace coin does not change the BitConnectX pitch.
